metadata.title: CMP/MARPOR standard coding scheme — full instruction-parity option space
metadata.source: Werner, Annika & Volkens, Andrea (2010). Manifesto Coding Instructions, 3rd fully revised edition (MARPOR/WZB), sections 4.2 and 8.
metadata.scope: 56 standard categories + 000 uncoded. Subcategories (handbook section 9, four-digit codes) are NOT used: the reliability study and this experiment restrict to the standard 56 + uncoded scheme (Mikhaylov, Laver & Benoit 2008, fn. 4).
metadata.purpose: This is the category list, definitions, and rile mapping offered to the models, mirroring what the MLB human coders selected from. It is the authoritative option space; the reduced 'categories' object inside cmp_coding_sample.json is a gold-coverage aid only.
metadata.rile_mapping_source: Mikhaylov, Laver & Benoit (2008) replication R (CMP_reliability_replication.R, lines 191-242). 13 left + 13 right + 31 none (000 = none).

000.label: Uncoded
000.definition: No category of the coding frame applies; the quasi-sentence cannot be fitted into the present scheme. 'Uncoded' does not mean the sentence is devoid of meaning. Code a sentence if at all possible; only use 000 after re-reading the definitions of categories in the relevant policy domains (Decision Rule 4).

101.label: Foreign Special Relationships: Positive
101.definition: Favourable mentions of particular countries with which the manifesto country has a special relationship (e.g. for Britain: former colonies); need for co-operation with and/or aid to such countries.

102.label: Foreign Special Relationships: Negative
102.definition: Negative mentions of particular countries with which the manifesto country has a special relationship; otherwise as 101, but negative.

103.label: Anti-Imperialism
103.definition: Negative references to exerting strong influence (political, military or commercial) over other states; negative references to controlling other countries as if part of an empire; favourable mentions of de-colonisation and of greater self-government/independence for colonies.

104.label: Military: Positive
104.definition: Need to maintain or increase military expenditure; modernising armed forces; rearmament and self-defence; keeping military treaty obligations; adequate military manpower; importance of external security.

105.label: Military: Negative
105.definition: Favourable mentions of decreasing military expenditures; disarmament; 'evils of war'; promises to reduce conscription; otherwise as 104, but negative.

106.label: Peace
106.definition: Peace as a general goal; belief in peace and peaceful means of solving crises; desirability of negotiations with hostile countries.

107.label: Internationalism: Positive
107.definition: Need for international co-operation; co-operation with countries other than those in 101; aid to developing countries; world planning of resources; international courts; support for the UN or any international goal/world state.

108.label: European Community/Union: Positive
108.definition: Favourable mentions of the EC/EU in general; desirability of expanding it or its competences, or of the manifesto country joining/remaining a member.

109.label: Internationalism: Negative
109.definition: Favourable mentions of national independence and sovereignty as opposed to internationalism; otherwise as 107, but negative.

110.label: European Community/Union: Negative
110.definition: Hostile mentions of the EC/EU; opposition to specific European policies or to the manifesto country's net contribution; otherwise as 108, but negative.

201.label: Freedom and Human Rights
201.definition: Favourable mentions of personal freedom and civil rights; freedom from bureaucratic control; freedom of speech; freedom from coercion in the political and economic spheres; individualism.

202.label: Democracy
202.definition: Favourable mentions of democracy as a method or goal in national and other organisations; involvement of all citizens in decision-making; generalised support for the manifesto country's democracy.

203.label: Constitutionalism: Positive
203.definition: Support for specific aspects of the constitution; use of constitutionalism as an argument for policy; general approval of the constitutional way of doing things.

204.label: Constitutionalism: Negative
204.definition: Opposition to the constitution in general or to specific aspects; otherwise as 203, but negative.

301.label: Decentralisation
301.definition: Support for federalism or devolution; more regional autonomy for policy or economy; keeping up local/regional customs and symbols; special consideration for local areas; deference to local expertise; territorial subsidiarity.

302.label: Centralisation
302.definition: Opposition to political decision-making at lower levels; support for more centralisation in political and administrative procedures; otherwise as 301, but negative.

303.label: Governmental and Administrative Efficiency
303.definition: Need for efficiency and economy in government and administration; cutting down the civil service; improving governmental procedures; making government cheaper and more effective. (Decision Rule 7: a specific policy position beats 303.)

304.label: Political Corruption
304.definition: Need to eliminate corruption, and associated abuse, in political and public life.

305.label: Political Authority
305.definition: Favourable mentions of strong government and government stability; the manifesto party's competence to govern and/or another party's lack of such competence. (Decision Rule 8: a specific policy position beats 305.)

401.label: Free Enterprise
401.definition: Favourable mentions of free enterprise capitalism; superiority of individual enterprise over state and control systems; private property rights, personal enterprise and initiative; unhampered individual enterprise.

402.label: Incentives
402.definition: Need for wage and tax policies to induce enterprise; encouragement to start enterprises; need for financial and other incentives such as subsidies.

403.label: Market Regulation
403.definition: Need for regulations to make private enterprise work better; actions against monopolies and trusts and in defence of consumers and small business; encouraging economic competition; social market economy.

404.label: Economic Planning
404.definition: Favourable mentions of long-standing economic planning of a consultative or indicative nature; need for government to create such a plan.

405.label: Corporatism
405.definition: Favourable mentions of the collaboration of employers and trade unions in overall economic planning through tripartite bodies of government, employers and trade unions.

406.label: Protectionism: Positive
406.definition: Favourable mentions of extension or maintenance of tariffs to protect internal markets; other domestic protectionism such as quota restrictions; export subsidies.

407.label: Protectionism: Negative
407.definition: Support for the concept of free trade; otherwise as 406, but negative.

408.label: Economic Goals
408.definition: Statements of intent to pursue economic goals not covered by other Domain 4 categories; a catch for overall interest in economics. Non-positional. (Decision Rule 10: a more specific policy position beats 408.)

409.label: Keynesian Demand Management
409.definition: Favourable mentions of demand-oriented economic policy; reducing depressions and/or increasing private demand through increased public demand or social expenditures.

410.label: Economic Growth
410.definition: Need to encourage or facilitate greater production; measures to aid this; importance of productivity to the economy; the paradigm of growth.

411.label: Technology and Infrastructure
411.definition: Importance of modernising industry, transport and communication; science and technological development in industry; need for training and research (not general education, see 506); public spending on infrastructure such as streets and harbours.

412.label: Controlled Economy
412.definition: General need for direct government control of the economy; control over prices, wages, rents, etc.; state intervention into the economic system.

413.label: Nationalisation
413.definition: Favourable mentions of government ownership, partial or complete, including government ownership of land.

414.label: Economic Orthodoxy
414.definition: Need for traditional economic orthodoxy (reduction of budget deficits, retrenchment in crisis, thrift and savings); support for traditional economic institutions such as the stock market and banking system; support for a strong currency.

415.label: Marxist Analysis
415.definition: Positive references (typically by communist parties) to the specific use of Marxist-Leninist terminology and analysis of situations that are otherwise uncodable.

416.label: Anti-Growth Economy
416.definition: Favourable mentions of anti-growth politics and steady-state economy; sustainable development.

501.label: Environmental Protection
501.definition: Preservation of countryside, forests, etc.; general preservation of natural resources against selfish interests; proper use of national parks; soil banks; environmental improvement.

502.label: Culture
502.definition: Need to provide cultural and leisure facilities including arts and sport; spending on museums, art galleries, etc.; encouraging worthwhile leisure activities and cultural mass media.

503.label: Social Justice
503.definition: Concept of equality; fair treatment of all people; special protection for the underprivileged; fair distribution of resources; removal of class barriers; end of discrimination (e.g. racial or sexual).

504.label: Welfare State Expansion
504.definition: Favourable mentions of need to introduce, maintain or expand any social service or social security scheme; support for social services such as health service or social housing. Excludes education.

505.label: Welfare State Limitation
505.definition: Limiting expenditure on social services or social security; favourable mentions of the social subsidiarity principle; otherwise as 504, but negative.

506.label: Education Expansion
506.definition: Need to expand and/or improve educational provision at all levels. Excludes technical training (coded 411).

507.label: Education Limitation
507.definition: Limiting expenditure on education; otherwise as 506, but negative.

601.label: National Way of Life: Positive
601.definition: Appeals to patriotism and/or nationalism; suspension of some freedoms to protect the state against subversion; support for established national ideas.

602.label: National Way of Life: Negative
602.definition: Against patriotism and/or nationalism; opposition to the existing national state; otherwise as 601, but negative.

603.label: Traditional Morality: Positive
603.definition: Favourable mentions of traditional moral values; prohibition, censorship and suppression of immorality and unseemly behaviour; maintenance and stability of family; religion.

604.label: Traditional Morality: Negative
604.definition: Opposition to traditional moral values; support for divorce, abortion, etc.; otherwise as 603, but negative.

605.label: Law and Order
605.definition: Enforcement of all laws; actions against crime; support and resources for police; tougher attitudes in courts; importance of internal security.

606.label: Social Harmony
606.definition: Appeal for national effort and solidarity; need for society to see itself as united; appeal for public spiritedness; decrying anti-social attitudes in times of crisis; support for the public interest; favourable mention of civil society. (Captures what you can do for your fellow citizens.)

607.label: Multiculturalism: Positive
607.definition: Favourable mentions of cultural diversity, communalism, cultural plurality and pillarization; preservation of autonomy of religious and linguistic heritages, including special educational provisions.

608.label: Multiculturalism: Negative
608.definition: Enforcement or encouragement of cultural integration; otherwise as 607, but negative.

701.label: Labour Groups: Positive
701.definition: Favourable references to labour groups, working class, the unemployed; support for trade unions; good treatment of manual and other employees.

702.label: Labour Groups: Negative
702.definition: Negative references to trade unions such as 'abuse of power'; otherwise as 701, but negative.

703.label: Agriculture and Farmers
703.definition: Support for agriculture and farmers; any policy aimed specifically at benefiting these. (Decision Rule 9 exception: ALL quasi-sentences devoted to agriculture are coded 703, even when a specific policy position such as 402 Incentives or 410 Economic Growth is used to further farmers' interests.)

704.label: Middle Class and Professional Groups
704.definition: Favourable references to the middle class and professional groups such as physicians or lawyers; old and new middle class.

705.label: Underprivileged Minority Groups
705.definition: Favourable references to underprivileged minorities defined neither in economic nor demographic terms, e.g. the handicapped, homosexuals, immigrants.

706.label: Non-economic Demographic Groups
706.definition: Favourable mentions of, or need for, assistance to women, old people, young people, linguistic groups, etc.; special interest groups of all kinds.
